summary: Eun Maeda (1855–1930) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Kozui Otani. He served as president (学長) of Toyo University and Ryukoku University.

Eun-su Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned her PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. She served as assistant professor at the University of Michigan until 2004, then became professor at Seoul National University.
Eunyoung Choe is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Korea University. She held a post as HK professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2015).

Eva K. Neumaier is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2006, she served as Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary and as Professor Emeritus, former Chair, and Professor at the University of Alberta.
Eva K. Neumaier-Dargyay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Rigzin. She held a position at the University of Calgary.

Eva Tichy is a linguist and Indologist. She earned her Dr. phil. under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nürnberg and completed her Habilitation at Marburg. Succeeding Helmut Rix in 1993, she held the Indo-European linguistics chair at Freiburg until 2017.

Eva Wilden is an Indologist who completed her MA, Promotion, and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She was a maître de conférences at EFEO from 2003 and became professor of Tamil and manuscript studies at Hamburg in 2017.

Evan Thompson is a philosopher who studied at Amherst College and the University of Toronto. He held posts at York University, the University of Toronto, and became Professor of Philosophy at the University of British Columbia in 2013.

Eviatar Shulman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from circa 1997 to 2008 and became chairman of its comparative religion department in 2009.

Eyal Aviv works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Utrecht and Leiden. Succeeding Jean Philippe Vogel, he served as professor of Sanskrit at Leiden University from 1939 to 1972 and founded the Indo-Iranian Journal in 1957.
Fa Qing is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a dissertation at the University of Calgary under doctoral supervisor Leslie S. Kawamura and interim supervisor Anthony W. Barber.

Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD under Pierre-Étienne Will at EHESS (1994–1999) and became a maître de conférences at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient circa 2001.

Fabio Rambelli is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied in Venice, Naples, and Tokyo. He taught at Sapporo University and was appointed to the Shinto Studies chair at UC Santa Barbara circa 2009.

Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the Federigo Enriques Department of Mathematics. She held posts at the University of Naples 'L'Orientale' (~1990–2000) and the University of Florence (~2000–2016).
Fafang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He served as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

Fang-kuei Li was a linguist, sinologist, and Tibetologist who studied at Michigan and Chicago under Edward Sapir. He held research and teaching posts at Academia Sinica, the University of Washington (1949–1969), and the University of Hawaiʻi (1969–1974).
Faren is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD from Lancaster University in 2008. In 2013, Faren was attested as a teaching consultant (教學顧問) at the University of Hong Kong.

Farzand Ali Durrani was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the Universities of Peshawar, the Punjab, and London. He served as a professor at the University of Peshawar from circa 1968 to 1993.
Fausto Gherardo Fumi was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Giuseppe Bardelli at the Scuola Normale Superiore (Classe di Lettere e Filosofia) from circa 1858 to 1862.
